title: Modeling Domain Objects
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of modeling domain objects using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates modeling domain objects.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Modeling Domain Objects** as part of **Advanced Properties and Class Modeling**. Classes group state and behavior; primary constructors and properties keep ordinary domain models concise, while initialization order still matters. Use the subtopics—Entities and Value Objects, Identifiers and Invariants, Representing Domain States with Types—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Entities and Value Objects
items.text: Entities and Value Objects should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.
